newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania tries two ex-communists over secret files.
newsitem.headline: Albania tries two ex-communists over secret files.

text.p: Two senior officials of Albania's former communist regime have appeared in court charged with destroying files compiled by the now-disbanded Sigurimi secret police, newspapers said on Thursday.
The daily Gazeta Shqiptare said the trial began on Wednesday against ex-deputy interior minister Vladimir Hysi and secret police chief Irakli Kocollari.

"They are charged with abuse of power and hampering the discovery of the truth," the daily said, adding Kocollari was also accused of crimes against humanity for ordering violence to be used while he was a prosecutor in southeastern Albania.
The charges relate to two key files -- one containing detailed information of the activities of the secret police outside Tirana, and the other undisclosed material.
Hysi and Kocollari headed the public order ministry and the secret police National Information Service (SHIK) respectively during 1991 and 1992, following Albania's first multi-party elections.

The reformed communist party won the first elections, changing its name to the Socialist Party before losing the second general election in March 1992 to the conservative Democratic Party led by President Sali Berisha.
